steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your component.
successCriteria: The code includes an import statement that imports React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package using an import statement.

steps.title: Create the ColorPicker component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ColorPicker that returns JSX. Use either function declaration or arrow function syntax with TypeScript.
steps.hint: Define a function called ColorPicker that returns some JSX (like a div).
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the ColorPicker component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A ColorPicker component function is defined and ready to be used.
successCriteria: The code contains a function named ColorPicker that returns JSX (e.g., a div).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ColorPicker component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a function named ColorPicker that returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ColorPicker component is not defined correctly. Ensure you create a function named ColorPicker that returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize color state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the ColorPicker component, initialize a state variable called 'color' using useState. Set the default value to '#000000' (black).
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to provide a type annotation for the state variable (string) and set the initial value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'color' initialized to '#000000', ready to track the selected color.
successCriteria: State variable named 'color' is declared
Uses useState hook
Initial value is '#000000'
Proper TypeScript typing (string)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the color state with useState. The component now tracks the selected color starting with black (#000000).
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you name the state variable 'color'? Is the initial value '#000000'? Did you use useState with proper TypeScript typing?
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's review: Inside the ColorPicker component, use useState to create a state variable called 'color' with initial value '#000000'. Remember to use TypeScript syntax.

steps.title: Define handleColorChange function
steps.instruction: Inside your ColorPicker component, define a function called handleColorChange that takes an event parameter of type React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> and updates the color state with the input's value.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives an event and calls setColor with event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleColorChange function that updates the color state when called with an input change event.
successCriteria: The code must include a function named handleColorChange that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and calls setColor with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the handleColorChange function that will update the color state when the input changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named exactly 'handleColorChange', takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter, and calls setColor with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleColorChange function is not defined correctly. Remember to create a function that takes an event parameter and updates the color state.

steps.title: Return a wrapper div
steps.instruction: In your ColorPicker component, return a <div> element from the component to wrap all future content.
steps.hint: Replace the existing return statement's content with a single <div> element. You can keep the existing comment inside it or remove it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a single <div> element that will serve as the wrapper for all UI elements.
successCriteria: The component's return statement contains exactly one <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the basic JSX structure for your ColorPicker component with a wrapper div.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure your component returns exactly one <div> element as the root.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a single <div> element. Check your return statement syntax.

steps.title: Add a heading for the color picker
steps.instruction: Inside the wrapper div, add an h1 element with the text 'Color Picker'.
steps.hint:

Color Picker

as the first element inside the opening
tag.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now displays a heading 'Color Picker' at the top of the color picker interface.
successCriteria: The wrapper div contains an h1 element with the exact text 'Color Picker'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a descriptive heading to your color picker component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a heading, but check if it's an h1 element with exactly 'Color Picker' as text.
steps.feedbackWrong:

steps.title: Add a color input element
steps.instruction: Inside the wrapper div, add an input element with type='color'.
steps.hint: Use the <input> tag with the type attribute set to 'color'. Place it after the heading.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding a color input
<input type='color' />
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now include a color input element that users can click to open a color picker.
successCriteria: input element
type='color'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a color input element. This will allow users to select colors visually.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added an input element with type='color' inside the div.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Add an input element with type='color' inside the wrapper div.

steps.title: Set the color input's value from state
steps.instruction: Set the value attribute of the existing color input element to the 'color' state variable.
steps.hint: Add value={color} to the <input> element to bind its value to the state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of binding an input value to state
<input type="text" value={textValue} onChange={handleChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The color input's value is now controlled by the component's state.
successCriteria: The <input> element has a value attribute
The value attribute is set to the 'color' state variable
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully bound the color input's value to the component state. This makes the input a controlled component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the value attribute to the existing input element and set it to the 'color' state variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The color input should have a value attribute that's bound to the 'color' state variable. Try adding value={color} to the input element.

steps.title: Wire the color input's onChange to handleColorChange
steps.instruction: Connect the color input's onChange event to the handleColorChange function by adding the onChange attribute to the input element.
steps.hint: Add onChange={handleColorChange} to the <input> element. This will call your handler whenever the color value changes.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of wiring an input's onChange to a handler
<input type='text' onChange={handleInputChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The color input will now call handleColorChange whenever the user selects a new color, updating the state accordingly.
successCriteria: The <input> element has an onChange attribute
The onChange attribute is set to handleColorChange
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully connected the color input's onChange event to your handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the onChange attribute to the input element and set it to call handleColorChange.
steps.feedbackWrong: The color input needs to have an onChange attribute that calls the handleColorChange function.

steps.instruction:

steps.title: Display the color value in the paragraph
steps.instruction: Inside the paragraph element, display the text 'Selected color: ' followed by the current color state value.
steps.hint: Use JSX interpolation with curly braces to include the color variable in the paragraph content.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of displaying state in a paragraph

Current value: {someState}
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph will show the current selected color value, updating whenever the color input changes.
successCriteria: Paragraph element contains text 'Selected color: '
Paragraph includes {color} interpolation
Text and variable are concatenated properly
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the current color value in the paragraph. The text will update automatically whenever the color changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the paragraph shows both the text 'Selected color: ' and the color value using proper JSX interpolation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph should display the text 'Selected color: ' followed by the current color value. Use JSX interpolation with curly braces to include the color variable.

steps.title: Add a color preview box
steps.instruction: Add a div element inside the wrapper div that uses the color state as its background color to create a visual preview of the selected color.
steps.hint: You can set the background color using the style attribute: style={{ backgroundColor: color }}. Make sure to also give the div some dimensions (like width and height) so it's visible.
steps.analogousExample: // Example of a color preview div
steps.expectedOutcome: A visual color preview box appears below the paragraph, showing the currently selected color as its background.
successCriteria: Add a div element inside the wrapper div
Set the div's style attribute to include backgroundColor: color
Include width and height properties in the style (e.g., '100px')
The div should be visible and display the current color
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added a visual color preview box that updates with the selected color.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a div, but make sure it has a style attribute with backgroundColor set to the color state, plus width and height properties so it's visible.
steps.feedbackWrong: The color preview box is missing or incomplete. Add a div element with style={{ backgroundColor: color, width: '100px', height: '100px' }} inside the wrapper div.
